page: Amazon Web Services x2idn.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance engineered for large-scale, memory-intensive enterprise workloads. The system is driven by dedicated Intel Xeon 8375C processors providing 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs operating at a 3.5 GHz clock speed on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware-assisted virtualization is supported via VMX directly on physical hardware, accompanied by instruction sets such as AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Hardware resource allocation features 2048 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, delivering a massive 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Attached storage includes 3800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps. The server operates without dedicated hardware GPUs.

Benchmark evaluation shows top-tier multi-threaded compute and encryption performance, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 87,902.84, a multi-core Geekbench score of 17,827.0, and 125,030.21 on stress-ng multi-core testing. Memory throughput registers at 334.29 GB/sec read and 133.98 GB/sec write on uncached 256MB blocks, with cached block reads reaching 6746.43 GB/sec. In-memory operations demonstrate strong scale, hitting 113.64 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and 30,985.99 on PassMark database operations.

While single-core metrics fall in the average tier—such as a 1,669.0 Geekbench single-core score—the massive parallel capability and dense RAM provide high cost efficiency for environments consolidating massive datasets. The architecture is suited for in-memory databases like SAP HANA and Redis, large relational database engines, electronic design automation (EDA), and heavy multi-threaded data processing.
